topic: Denominator-locked completeness for conditional causal effects in selected COPAGs. Fix a finite input-free COPAG over binary observed variables representing Chen--Mooij's positive discrete SCM class with arbitrary latent and selection variables, disjoint Y,X,C, and positive selected conditioning strata. Define Branch-sCIDP to enumerate every reachable role state using the source algorithm's current bucket intersections and valid Rule-2 exchanges, run sIDP on each terminal joint P(Y,Cbar | do(Xbar),S=1), and normalize any successful functional. Prove Branch-sCIDP succeeds iff P(Y | do(X),C,S=1) is identified; otherwise construct a denominator-locked selected conditional hedge: a represented MAG/sADMG and terminal-joint forest plus explicit positive rational binary SCMs with the same full selected observational law and the same positive conditioning denominator but different joint numerators. Give a shared-cache O(3^n poly(n)+output) formula-or-certificate algorithm and verification polynomial in graph plus expanded rational certificate size. Consumer: extend PAGId from no-selection conditional identification to formula-or-checkable-failure output for selected-cohort FCI/PAG analyses. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Varying one rational interior mechanism makes all fixed-regime masses affine; equality of the normalized selected observational law and conditioning denominator becomes a homogeneous rational system Av=0, while numerator disagreement is a row b outside row(A), so a locked witness exists exactly when rank([A;b]) exceeds rank(A). Exact enumeration produced a selected binary bow with identical observational laws, denominator 1/2, numerators 9/25 versus 7/23, and conditional effects 18/25 versus 14/23. It also verified both four-cycle graph realizations and exact cancellation of their conditional ratios. Checks corrected whole-bucket moves to role intersections, separated the independent-root cancellation model from the actual hedge realization, tested positivity and boundary cases, and found no current primary-source collision. These are derived special cases, not the complete converse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that failure at every reachable terminal state forces a represented residual forest from which one can construct positive rational binary mechanisms sharing the selected observational law and conditioning denominator while separating the numerator, with the advertised output-sensitive synthesis bound. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively enumerate input-free COPAGs on at most four observed vertices and their exact Rule-2 role-state graphs; any graph-valid identifying formula for an all-branches-fail conditional target refutes completeness, while a proof that all compatible rational binary pairs at a failing graph violate denominator locking refutes the certificate coordinate. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_selected_pag_conditional_hedge.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Is a branch-complete version of sCIDP complete for positive discrete input-free COPAG queries P(Y | do(X), C, S=1), with every all-branches failure yielding a denominator-locked selected conditional hedge realized by positive rational binary SCMs?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sound sCIDP for conditional effects under selection, leaves completeness to future work, and says an appropriate conditional hedge analogue is likely required.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: CIDP is sound and complete for conditional causal-effect identification from PAGs without selection, providing the closest completed conditional-PAG analogue.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: For a specified semi-Markovian graph, conditional interventional distributions have a complete identification algorithm based on action-observation exchange followed by joint identification.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser and Judea Pearl

open_problems.why_unsolved: Chen and Mooij prove completeness only for unconditional selected interventional kernels on input-free COPAGs. Their conditional algorithm applies a particular sequence of Rule-2 exchanges before sIDP, and they explicitly leave completeness and the correct conditional hedge criterion open. Jaber et al. solve the no-selection PAG problem, but that converse does not have to preserve a selected conditioning denominator. Searches for the specific target-method pair—denominator-locked or selected conditional hedges—found no existing construction. The missing proof step is to turn simultaneous failure over all reachable exchange states into one represented MAG/sADMG witness whose two positive models agree on the complete selected observational law and the denominator while disagreeing on the joint numerator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if identification theorem for branch-enumerated sCIDP, with a constructive residual-forest-to-positive-rational-binary-SCM map fixing P(C | do(X), S=1), separating P(Y,C | do(X), S=1), and yielding a checkable formula-or-certificate algorithm with an explicit output-sensitive complexity bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact selected-PAG model, separates unconditional completeness from conditional soundness, and explicitly lands on the missing conditional hedge criterion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: FCI returns a PAG while latent selection remains causally relevant -> sIDP completely identifies unconditional selected kernels on COPAGs -> conditioning can identify ratios whose corresponding joint is not identifiable -> completeness requires a conditional denominator-preserving failure witness

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the sIDP residual tuple, represented-MAG construction, and selected-forest nonidentifiability proof, strengthening the proof to coordinate every terminal role state and preserve a common denominator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already converts unconditional sIDP failure on a COPAG into a represented selected graphical obstruction, which is precisely the construction the conditional converse must refine.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the complete conditional-PAG action-observation exchange analysis and its reduction of a ratio query to terminal joint-identification calls.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It resolves the same conditional-versus-joint mismatch under Markov equivalence, but without latent selection or denominator locking.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply recursive influence-function construction for an identified PAG functional, followed by cross-fitting and a delta-method normalization step.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful branch returns a finite observed-law functional whose normalized conditional value has the same functional-differentiation structure.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp identified set for a discrete conditional selected-cohort effect P(Y | do(X), C, S=1) over all positive SCMs represented by a given MAG or PAG when point identification fails?

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly proposes a complete method for sharp discrete bounds in MAGs and PAGs under selection bias as future work.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: The paper derives systematic analytic bounds for causal effects over PAG equivalence classes, but does not incorporate latent selection.
source_refs.author: Alexis Bellot

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal queries involving confounding, selection, and missingness reduce to polynomial programs that produce sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds for a specified causal model.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bellot exploits PAG invariants but omits selection, whereas Duarte et al. accommodate selection in a fixed discrete causal specification but do not optimize uniformly over every MAG/sADMG represented by a PAG or provide a graph-native sharpness criterion for that union. Chen and Mooij explicitly identify sharp discrete bounds under selection as open. For a conditional effect the objective is a ratio, and positive conditioning strata couple the numerator and denominator; the first new step is to encode both PAG-represented model uncertainty and selected-law constraints in one fractional-polynomial feasible set and prove its extrema are attainable within, or sharply approached by, the positive model class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-indexed characterization and terminating optimization algorithm whose output interval equals the infimum and supremum of P(Y | do(X), C, S=1) over all compatible positive discrete SCMs represented by the MAG/PAG, with an attaining sequence or exact rational endpoint certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames partial identification as an immediate next question after establishing the selected-PAG point-identification boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A selected PAG can leave a causal query nonidentified -> a failure certificate establishes multiplicity but gives no magnitude -> discrete positivity may still restrict feasible effects -> compute the sharp graph- and selected-law-specific interval

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the use of invariant PAG structure to avoid naive enumeration of every represented causal graph while adding selection constraints and a ratio objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It addresses causal ranges under the same equivalence-class uncertainty, lacking the selected-cohort semantics.

method_exemplars.technique: Use response-function parameterization, polynomial equality constraints, dual relaxations, and spatial branch-and-bound to certify discrete bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired endpoints are extrema of a rational conditional functional over observationally indistinguishable positive discrete SCMs, matching the polynomial-program framework after denominator clearing.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over support-function inference and uniform Gaussian approximation for estimated sharp-bound endpoints under sample selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Although its identifying assumptions differ, it supplies explicit limit theory and confidence procedures for selection-bound endpoints, the inferential object produced by the proposed graphical method.

open_problems.open_problem: Does selected conditional identification admit a complete formula-or-hedge characterization for iCOPAGs or general iSOPAGs with input nodes, rather than only input-free COPAGs?

source_refs.claim: The input-aware iSOPAG calculus and sCIDP construction are sound, whereas the stated sIDP completeness theorem assumes an input-free COPAG and conditional completeness remains open.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: The ioSCM calculus handles inputs, cycles, latent confounding, and selection and extends ID, but does not establish the selected conditional equivalence-class completeness result.
source_refs.author: Patrick Forré and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: Conditional effects have a complete algorithm for input-free MPDAGs with observed variables, showing that equivalence-class uncertainty and background knowledge need not preclude completeness.
source_refs.author: Sara LaPlante and Emilija Perković

open_problems.why_unsolved: Chen and Mooij's theorem boundary is explicit: selected-kernel completeness is proved for P=(∅,V), while the input-node theory supplies sound invariant id-separations and identification rules but not the corresponding global conditional converse. Input kernels strengthen the observational equivalence that a witness pair must preserve, so the represented-MAG/selected-forest construction is the first proof step that changes: it must preserve every input-indexed selected kernel rather than one selected observational distribution. The scan found input-aware causal calculi and a complete observed-variable MPDAG conditional algorithm, but no complete selected conditional iCOPAG/iSOPAG formula-or-certificate result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a completeness theorem producing an input-kernel-preserving conditional hedge whenever every legal exchange-and-sIDP branch fails, or a smallest iCOPAG/iSOPAG counterexample proving that the input-free branching characterization is insufficient.

writing_exemplar.why: Its hierarchy of iSOPAG soundness, input-free COPAG completeness, and conditional future work gives the cleanest scope-boundary narrative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Inputs encode experiments or background knowledge in a learned ancestral graph -> the selected causal calculus remains sound with inputs -> global completeness is proved only after removing inputs -> characterize whether conditional completeness survives input-indexed observational constraints

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize invariant id-separation, Rule L2, and residual-forest representation while retaining input-node kernel semantics in both indistinguishable models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The paper contains both sides of the gap: an input-aware sound calculus and an input-free completeness construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use transitional kernels and sigma-separation to track interventions as explicit inputs throughout marginalization, conditioning, and fixing arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its ioSCM machinery is designed for input-indexed causal kernels under latent selection, although it lacks the required equivalence-class converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively differentiate a successful input-indexed identifying functional and use cross-fitted nuisance estimates to construct an asymptotically linear estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful input-aware formula remains a composition of observed kernels, making PAG-DML the nearest generic inference construction.

open_problems.open_problem: Can normalized sCIDP functionals for positive discrete selected PAGs be estimated efficiently, with valid confidence intervals accounting jointly for numerator-denominator normalization and uncertainty from learning the PAG?

source_refs.claim: The paper states that efficiency, improved estimators, and discover-then-estimate validity for selected-PAG functionals remain unstudied.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: The no-selection PAG paper identifies conditional effects but does not supply efficiency or post-discovery inference for selected conditional functionals.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Resampling and screening provide asymptotically valid post-causal-discovery confidence sets mainly in PC/DAG settings, not for selected FCI/PAG functionals.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, and Daniel Malinsky

open_problems.why_unsolved: PAG-DML derives influence functions for identifiable functionals in a fixed given PAG, while current post-discovery inference primarily treats PC/DAG adjustment targets. A branch-selected sCIDP formula is a data-dependent composition of selected-law kernels and a ratio whose denominator may approach zero; learning an FCI/PAG can also change the successful branch and therefore the reported functional. The missing argument must establish pathwise differentiability and an efficient influence function for the normalized selected functional, then control graph and branch selection so coverage targets the fixed causal effect rather than a data-selected surrogate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator for every successful normalized sCIDP functional with an explicit efficient influence function, asymptotic linearity and efficiency bound under stated positivity rates, plus a discover-then-estimate confidence procedure with pointwise or uniform coverage for the fixed selected-cohort causal effect.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion cleanly separates graphical identification, estimator efficiency, and validity after causal discovery under latent selection.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: sIDP or sCIDP returns an observed-law functional from a selected PAG -> identification alone does not control sampling behavior -> normalization and learned-graph branching create additional instability -> derive efficient estimation and coverage for the fixed selected causal target

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively derive an influence function from a PAG identification expression and construct a cross-fitted debiased estimator with product-rate remainder control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest generic estimator theory for graph-identified PAG functionals, but it does not handle selected conditional formulas.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt randomized resampling and screening of conditional-independence tests and the union-of-intervals coverage proof from PC/DAGs to FCI/PAG branch outputs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses the distinction between inference for a fixed causal effect and inference for a data-selected graphical functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the conditional-PAG decomposition and normalization structure to expose the primitive nuisance kernels whose derivatives must be combined.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its complete no-selection CIDP formula has the same quotient and branch structure before selected-law factors are introduced.

open_problems.open_problem: Can global strict positivity in selected COPAG conditional identification be replaced by a necessary-and-sufficient formula-specific support condition that still licenses every Rule-L2 exchange and final normalization?

source_refs.claim: The selected-PAG pointwise theory uses positive continuous kernels, while positive discrete SCMs provide the class used for its completeness witness.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: The paper develops graphical and formula-specific positivity conditions that license causal identification formulas without requiring a globally positive observational law.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, and Sanghack Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hwang et al. analyze positivity requirements for do-calculus and Q-decomposition in a specified causal graph, while Chen and Mooij use positivity and continuity to make selected conditioning kernels pointwise well-defined across a PAG-represented class. The scan found no positivity-aware CIDP or sCIDP result combining latent selection with Markov equivalence. The first proof step that changes is the use of globally positive canonical conditionals in Rule L2: these must be replaced by support-restricted versions that agree across every represented MAG and remain valid along all branch states, followed by a proof that the final selected conditioning denominator is positive exactly where the functional is evaluated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient graphical and algebraic support criterion for a specified selected conditional query, together with a positivity-aware Branch-sCIDP algorithm returning either a pointwise identifying functional on its maximal support or a counterexample proving that no such pointwise functional exists.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination model and makes positivity central to pointwise conditioning and completeness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selected-PAG identification repeatedly forms conditional kernels -> global positivity guarantees these operations but may exclude identifiable boundary laws -> formula-specific positivity exists for known graphs without selection -> characterize the exact support needed for selected conditional PAG identification

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate positivity obligations through do-calculus, marginalization, factorization, and Q-decomposition to obtain a formula-specific observed-law condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed result needs the same proof-level bookkeeping, extended from one known graph to every MAG represented by a selected PAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the positive-continuous-kernel conditioning lemmas used by Rule L2 with support-indexed conditional kernels and trace their compatibility through the assembly tree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those lemmas are the precise point where the existing selected-PAG proof consumes global positivity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use influence-function recursion with explicit overlap factors to derive rates and limit laws on the maximal identified support.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A support-aware identifying formula needs inference whose remainder bounds expose how near-zero selected denominators affect regularity.

literature_map:
Chen and Mooij (2026, arXiv:2603.26301) give a measure-theoretic selected-PAG calculus and complete sIDP for unconditional kernels on input-free COPAGs.
The same paper presents sound sCIDP for conditional selected kernels but explicitly leaves completeness and an appropriate conditional hedge criterion open.
Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij (2024, arXiv:2401.06925) formalize latent selection by conditioning SCMs and establish compatibility with marginalization and intervention.
Forré and Mooij (2020, UAI; arXiv:1901.00433) handle inputs, cycles, latent confounding, and selection through ioSCMs, without the target selected conditional equivalence-class converse.
Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022, NeurIPS; arXiv:2202.12263) complete conditional identification for PAGs without selection.
Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, NeurIPS) introduced CIDP and highlighted conditional effects identifiable even when the corresponding joint is not.
Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, ICML) provide the unconditional PAG completeness and graphical failure characterization inherited by later work.
Shpitser and Pearl (2006, UAI) give complete conditional identification for a specified semi-Markovian graph; their joint-ID work supplies the classical hedge benchmark.
Huang and Valtorta (2006, UAI) establish completeness of do-calculus, the fixed-graph benchmark for subsequent PAG completeness arguments.
Bareinboim, Tian, and Pearl (2014, AAAI; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v28i1.9074) give complete recovery of observational conditionals under selection.
Bareinboim and Tian (2015, AAAI; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v29i1.9679) study causal-effect recovery under combined confounding and selection, with completeness restricted to the Markovian case.
Bellot (2024, UAI; arXiv:2311.07259) bounds causal effects over PAG equivalence classes without selection, while Duarte et al. (2024, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) give polynomial-program sharp bounds for fixed discrete causal specifications that may include selection.
Hwang et al. (2024, ICML) develop formula-specific positivity conditions, but not for selected PAG or COPAG branching.
Jung, Tian, and Bareinboim (2021, ICML) derive DML estimators from identified PAG functionals, while Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2026, Biometrika; arXiv:2405.06763) address post-discovery coverage mainly for PC/DAG settings.
No located primary source occupied the denominator-locked selected conditional hedge target or supplied a formula-or-checkable-failure completeness theorem for selected conditional COPAG queries.
